claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on a narrow basis because aggregate readiness passed, rollout is limited and reversible, and policy compliance can be satisfied through explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure plus monitoring despite the exposed weak public-benefits eligibility segment.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
Policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Rollout monitoring, rollback capability, and limited percentage are not substitutes for disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or equivalent launch artifact showing explicit disclosure of the public benefits eligibility limitation.
Provide approval evidence for that disclosure before launch, if approval is required in this process.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide an approved risk-acceptance record that expressly covers the public benefits eligibility exposure.
If relying on exclusion as mitigation, provide rollout gating evidence showing the affected use case is actually excluded from the launch cohort.
specific_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on residency documentation guidance.
The available risk-acceptance draft is not approved.
The draft does not address the public benefits eligibility exposure.
Policy says rollout controls and small-percentage launch do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure has actually been completed or approved.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action to certify the model is currently evidentially supported.
Any implication that rollout controls alone make the launch compliant.
Any implication that approved risk acceptance covers the exposed public benefits eligibility segment.
